title: £1 Million by 60: Start at 20, 30 or 40? The Monthly Cost 💷🤯 #shorts
description:
How much a month to have £1 million by 60? It depends hugely on when you start.

At an assumed 7% a year in a Stocks & Shares ISA:
• Lucy starts at 20: about £405 a month. Pays in about £194,000, growth does about 81%
• Tom starts at 30: about £855 a month. Pays in about £308,000
• Maya starts at 40: about £1,970 a month. Pays in about £473,000, growth does about half
Every 10 years of waiting more than doubles the monthly cost.

The twist: with 2% inflation a year (the Bank of England's target), £1 million in 40 years is worth about £453,000 in today's money.

One thing people miss: the ISA allowance is £20,000 a year (about £1,667 a month), so starting at 40 you'd need a pension as well.

Your turn: starting at 25, how much a month would you need? Comment your guess 👇

Sources: gov.uk/individual-savings-accounts · bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy

Illustration only. Assumes 7% a year after fees, compounded monthly, paid in at the end of each month until 60. Investments can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you put in. General education, not financial advice.

Music and sound effects: original, made for this channel.

assumptions: 7% a year effective after fees, compounded monthly, contributions at the end of each month until age 60
Monthly needed for £1,000,000: £404.61 from 20, £855.10 from 30, £1,970.30 from 40
Inflation 2% a year (BoE target): £1,000,000 in 40 years = £452,890 in today's money
ISA allowance £20,000 a year = £1,666.67 a month
From 25 (comment-question answer, not shown): £584.31 a month
